_about: Behaviour seen at runtime that the generated reference does not show.
tools/gen_api.py stamps each entry into the block and the index line of the call it names.
name: a module function (apex.module.function) or a method on the class that declares it
(apex.module.Class.method; see api/methods-index.md). A name not in the reference stops the build.
kind: raises | silent | note. observed: the Apex release it was seen in.
Add an entry only for behaviour that was actually observed, and say how.

overrides.name: apex.catalog.createPropertiesElement3DHomogeneous
overrides.behaviour: Raises `RuntimeError: ERROR: THIS FUNCTION IS DEPRECATED AND WILL BE REMOVED IN THE FUTURE RELEASE.` The reference does not mark it deprecated.

overrides.name: apex.attribute.Properties3DModel.update
overrides.behaviour: `elementProperties3D={"MID": <Material object>}` is accepted without error and ignored: `getProperties()` shows no MID afterwards.
overrides.instead: Pass the material's integer id, `{"MID": material.id}`. `PropertiesElement3D.getReferenceMaterial()` then returns the material.

overrides.name: apex.studies.LoadCaseItem.getCommand
overrides.behaviour: On a `SubcaseNastran`, `getCommand(commandName="LOAD").setValue(n)` reads back correctly in the same script but is gone by the next script, so the exported subcase has no `LOAD =`. Calling `setCommand` before `setValue` does not keep it either. Seen through a remote bridge that runs each script as a separate call; not yet reproduced in the Apex script editor. Output requests are not subcase commands: `getCommand(commandName="DISPLACEMENT")` (also `STRESS`, `SPCFORCES`) raises `Command 'DISPLACEMENT' is UNSUPPORTED`.
overrides.instead: `cmd = subcase.getCommand(commandName="LOAD"); cmd.setValue(load.id); subcase.setCommand(commandName="LOAD", activate=True)`, in that order, then read the value back in a later script or in the exported deck.

overrides.name: apex.studies.LoadCaseItem.setCommand
overrides.behaviour: `setCommand(commandName=..., activate=True)` called after `getCommand(...).setValue(...)` is what made a subcase case control value persist. `commandName` is the bare command name: `"LOAD = 2"` raises `Command 'LOAD = 2' is UNSUPPORTED`.

overrides.name: apex.geometry.createCurve
overrides.behaviour: There is no part argument. The curve was created in the part made most recently (a part created with `Assembly.createPart` just before), not in the part of the input locations.
overrides.instead: Create or activate the target part immediately before `createCurve`, and check `curve.getPathName()` afterwards.

overrides.name: apex.attribute.createNodeTie
overrides.behaviour: The tie is created at assembly level as `Node Tie <id>`. It has `name` and `getName()` but no rename: no `setName`, and `update()` takes no `name`. With `distributionType=apex.attribute.DistributionType.Rigid` and `dependentDoF="123456"` it exported as an RBE2.
overrides.instead: Keep the returned `NodeTie` objects (or their ids) in a dict keyed by your own names.

overrides.name: apex.attribute.createInteractionManualPair
overrides.behaviour: The new pair has no representation: `getActiveRep()` returns `None` until `createInteractionRep(...)` is called on it, so it is not yet a glue or a contact.
overrides.instead: `pair.createInteractionRep(name=..., interactionType=apex.attribute.InteractionType.Glue, interactionPropertyGeometric=geo)`. In SOL 101 the subcases also need `BCONTACT`; see pitfalls.md.
